texts.orig: Malachite is a basic cupric carbonate,  represented by the formula CuCO;Cu(HO)e, and has usually been formed by the action of meteoric agencies on other   copper-minerals; hence ỉt is found in the upper of ore-deposits; often an incrustation, and occasionally as a pseudomorph after cuprite, chalcocite, &c. When formed, as commonly bappens; by the alteration of copper-pyrites the iron of this mineral usually takes the form of limonite, which may remain associated with the malachite. Occasionally, though but rarely , malachite occurs in small dark green prismatic crystals of the monoclinic system. Its usual nodular OI stalagmitic forms, with mammillated, reniform or botryoidal surface, whilst in other cases ỉt forms fbrous, compact OI even earthy masses. Tbe nodules, though commonly dull on the outside, may display on fracture a beautiful zonary structure; the successive layers often succeeding each other as curved deposits of light and dark tints The colours include various shades of apple-green, grass-green , emerald-green and verdigris-green. Certain varieties exhibit finely fibrous structure,   producing on the fractured surface soft silky sheen. part
